defect.description: Isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO) never matches a real file: typing.TextIO is not a base class of what open() returns (io.TextIOWrapper, or the io.BufferedWriter of the default os.devnull log), so stop() still leaves every file log open, as before; it should test io.IOBase (or for a close method).

review_items: isinstance(log_output, TextIO) is always False for file objects, so string-path log files are never closed
Default devnull BufferedWriter is not matched by either check, so the devnull fd leaks on stop()
Exceptions from close()/os.close() skip process termination; try/except safety was removed
Calling stop() twice with an fd log raises EBADF because os.close is not idempotent
log_output != PIPE compares by value; use `is not PIPE`
votes.evidence_quote: `isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO)` returns `False` for all file objects. `typing.TextIO` is a generic alias; on Python 3.8 it does not match `_io.TextIOWrapper` or `_io.BufferedWriter` at runtime. A string-path log (`log_output="driver.log"`) opens a `TextIOWrapper` — the `isinstance` check fails, and the file is never closed.
votes.justification: The review names the same cause: typing.TextIO does not match TextIOWrapper or BufferedWriter at runtime. It names the same effect at the same spot in stop(): file logs are never closed, including the devnull default.
